subject: Recap + Proposed Eval Framework and Kickoff Plan for NimbleCare POC
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@nimblecare.health>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@nimblecare.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + Proposed Eval Framework and Kickoff Plan for NimbleCare POC

Hi Tom & Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a concrete proposal for a short, measurable POC so we can validate latency/cost and the integration surface with your triage workflow. High level: you want to reduce average response latency for assisted-notes generation, measure hallucination rate relative to current templates, and understand monthly cost at expected volume (approx 120k tokens/day).

Proposed success criteria (initial):
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 120ms for the 1–2k token responses in your busiest route.
- Quality: hallucination incidents <= 3% on our evaluation prompts (we'll supply the seed set).
- Cost: projected per-1M-token unit cost below $X (we'll provide modeled numbers based on batching/quantization).

POC timeline (proposed, 4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (this week): kickoff + access + runbook delivery.
2) Week 1: integration of API and sample dataset ingest; baseline metrics captured.
3) Week 2: performance tuning (batching, KV cache) + quality tuning on prompt set.
4) Week 3: load test, final readout, and next-step recommendation.

Ownership:
- Connor (me): POC PM and customer point-of-contact / business metrics.
- Marissa (SE): technical integration, runbook walkthrough, latency tuning.
- Dylan (CS): onboarding/training, acceptance criteria and success gating.

Actions I want to confirm this week:
- Your side: provide a representative prompt set (5–10 templates) + sample telemetry for one busy route by Wed 7/15.
- We'll: share a POC runbook (attached) and a draft quote for the POC resources.

I attached the runbook (nimblecare-poc-runbook_v1.pdf) and the estimated quote (redwood-proposal-july2026.xlsx). Let me know if the success criteria above capture the right priorities or if you want alternate thresholds. If that looks good, we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff on Tue 7/14 or Wed 7/15 — what works best for you?

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Connors mobile: (415) 555-0132

Attachments: nimblecare-poc-runbook_v1.pdf (13 pages, runbook outline), redwood-proposal-july2026.xlsx (POC resource/estimate)

From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@nimblecare.health>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap + Proposed Eval Framework and Kickoff Plan for NimbleCare POC

Thanks Connor — that looks like a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The "assisted-notes" route is our priority; typical responses are 300–900 tokens, but edge cases hit ~2k. We can provide logs for a week (anonymized).
- For quality, we care about "incorrect clinical suggestions" primarily — we'll mark those during the readout. 3% seems reasonable as a target to start.
- For cost, can you provide a scenario that includes a dedicated pool vs hosted at burst capacity? We need a side-by-side to evaluate procurement.

We can do kickoff Tue 7/14 at 10:00 AM PT. I'll upload the prompt templates and a 5,000-record anonymized log export to the shared Drive by EOD 7/14.

Priya
VP Product, NimbleCare

Great — calendar invite sent for Tue 7/14 10:00 AM PT. Attached is a slightly revised runbook (nimblecare-poc-runbook_v1.pdf) with a short integration checklist and test data expectations. Highlights:

- Integration checklist (high level): API key provisioning, sample payload schema, rate limits, and a small ingress adapter we can drop into your staging.
- Test harness: we'll run a 2-hour baseline job to capture latency and token costs using a 1% synthetic traffic mirror before full ingest.
- Acceptance gating: both quality and latency gates must pass in the final load test window; if latency gate fails but quality exceeds target, we'll propose a fallback model variant for the final week.

Marissa, can you confirm the adapter language (Node/Java/Python) and who will own the staging-side env?

Tom/Priya — quick ask: if you can confirm who will be the engineering point-of-contact on your side, we can send the staging adapter and the API key this afternoon.

Thanks,
Connor

Following up from the kickoff call — couple of technical notes and owners after the walkthrough: 

- Integration adapter: we provide Node and Python. We'll drop the package in the shared Drive. Owner (NimbleCare): Dev lead to be named; temporary contact will be Tom for staging access.
- Data/QA: please confirm that the telemetry export will include timestamps and route identifiers. This is required for our per-route latency breakdown.
- Performance tuning tasks (Marissa):
  * Day 1–2: baseline test + KV cache warm-up; collect token distributions.
  * Day 3–5: batching config sweep (batch size, timeout) to hit P95 target.
  * Day 6–7: quantization profile test on a small set of weight-shared models (if customer approves).

- Acceptance tasks (Dylan): build the readout deck and the evaluation script for hallucination detection (we'll seed it with 150 evaluation prompts).

I'll prep the tech checklist and post it to Drive by EOD 7/16. Connor — I noted Priya's request for cost scenarios; I'll add a short section showing dedicated vs hosted assumptions.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Connor/Marissa/Dylan —

Thanks for the clear plan and the runbook. We uploaded the anonymized 5k log export and the 10 prompt templates to the shared Drive (link in HubSpot). Our dev lead is Suresh Patel (suresh.patel@nimblecare.health) — he'll own staging. We'll expect the staging API key this afternoon.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you include a short checklist for SOC/PII handling in the runbook so our compliance team can sign off quickly?
2) For the dedicated vs hosted cost scenarios, please include an expected break-even token volume and a note about reserved vs burst pricing.

If those two items are included, NimbleCare is comfortable moving forward with the 4-week cadence you described. Looking forward to the load test.

Tom
